# PyAutoGalaxy Assistant

> The front door of the PyAutoGalaxy Assistant — an AI assistant for doing galaxy structure and morphology science with PyAutoGalaxy: agent instructions, task skills and a reference wiki in one repository that you drive in natural language from inside an AI coding agent. It routes by intent: set up, see what the assistant can do, read the reference, or jump to runnable examples.

## How to use it

The assistant is supported **only inside an AI coding agent** that can read this repository and execute Python: **Claude Code** or **Codex** (recommended and tested), or **OpenCode** as an experimental alternative. Clone the repository and open the agent inside it — `AGENTS.md` (via `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code) loads automatically and nothing else is needed:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autogalaxy_assistant.git
cd autogalaxy_assistant
claude        # or: codex / opencode
```

Then paste one of the two starter prompts in the [README](./README.md). Desktop and IDE versions of these agents are fine when they provide the same repository and execution access. Browser chats with a GitHub connector are **no longer supported** (retired 2026-09-10; see [`docs/archive/`](./docs/archive/)).

Agentic does not mean autonomous: you can ask questions, plan an analysis or learn in **Teacher Mode** without running anything — say so in your prompt.

## If you are an agent reading this file

Read order: [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) → [skills/README.md](./skills/README.md) → the relevant skill → [wiki/](./wiki).

**⚠️ API currency — read before writing any PyAutoGalaxy code.** Older PyAutoGalaxy releases are heavily represented in model training data and their API is **out of date**. Do **not** write PyAutoGalaxy from memory — mirror the matching skill and verify symbols against the installed library (`dir()`, or `python autoassistant/audit_skill_apis.py --code "<snippet>"` on a harness without the PreToolUse code gate). The single most common stale error: **plotting is functional now.** Use `aplt.subplot_fit_imaging(fit=fit, output_path=..., output_format="png")` and `aplt.subplot_imaging_dataset(dataset=..., output_path=..., output_filename=..., output_format="png")` — note that `output_filename` is accepted by the dataset subplots, `plot_array` and `plot_grid`, but **not** by `subplot_fit_imaging`, which writes a fixed `fit.png` into `output_path` (passing it raises `TypeError`). The old object-oriented plotters — `aplt.FitImagingPlotter`, `aplt.ImagingPlotter`, `aplt.GalaxyPlotter`, `aplt.GalaxiesPlotter`, `aplt.InversionPlotter` — and the `aplt.MatPlot2D` / `aplt.Include2D` / `aplt.Output` configuration objects have all been **removed**; never emit them. The whole plotting surface is module-level functions, and `dir(autogalaxy.plot)` is the authoritative list.

**⚠️ This assistant is young, but it is complete.** Twenty-seven skills exist: the nine-skill core modelling loop (environment, data preparation, simulation, model building, search configuration, running the fit, plotting, results, debugging), the eight **feature** skills beyond a single smooth profile (bases and MGE, pixelisations, extra galaxies / sky / operated profiles, ellipse fitting, multi-dataset, interferometry, multi-galaxy and clusters, search chaining), two output surfaces (script→notebook, the read-only results-inspector MCP server), two meta, two project-workflow, one literature and three maintenance. The reference wiki, the four-card benchmark suite and the `hpc/` folder are all in place. What is *young* is the evidence: **no benchmark run has been scored yet** (`benchmarks/RESULTS.md` says so), so do not cite benchmark performance. [`skills/README.md`](./skills/README.md) is the index of what exists and [`ROADMAP.md`](./ROADMAP.md) is what is still wished for; **never describe anything on the roadmap as though you had read it**, and when a question falls outside the skills and wiki, answer from the installed source or the `autogalaxy_workspace` script and say that is what you did.

## Agent instructions (canonical)

- [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md): safety rules, modes, and repository conventions — the source of truth.

## What it can do

- [skills/README.md](./skills/README.md): all twenty-seven skills that exist, then the short backlog of two that deliberately do not.

## The bundled dataset

- `dataset/imaging/cosj100020+015344/` — a real four-band JWST/NIRCam cutout (F115W, F150W at 0.03"/pix; F277W, F444W at 0.06"/pix) of a bright early-type galaxy at spectroscopic z = 0.3422, reduced from COSMOS-Web exposures. Both README starter prompts point at it, so you can answer a real question without the user supplying data. Three things to carry honestly, all documented in [its README](./dataset/imaging/cosj100020+015344/README.md): the **sky is not subtracted** (a positive pedestal 4.5–19x the noise — free `background_sky_level` on an `af.Model(ag.DatasetModel)` or subtract the measured value), the shipped **PSF is a model (STPSF) kernel** and is the dominant systematic, and a **faint neighbour sits 2.6" from the centre**, inside any useful mask. The layout and the `info.json` schema are in [wiki/core/operations/dataset.md](./wiki/core/operations/dataset.md). Plot it and settle the mask extent and contaminants with the user before composing any fit; if you cannot execute code in this session, ask the user to plot it and report back — the gate is never waived.

## Reference

- [wiki/core/index.md](./wiki/core/index.md): curated PyAuto\* reference. The `stack/`, `api/`, `concepts/`, `operations/` and `external/` sections are all complete; the index lists every page and states what "complete" does and does not claim.
- [wiki/literature/index.md](./wiki/literature/index.md): the galaxy-structure science wiki — concepts (Sersic profiles, bulge–disk decomposition, MGE, isophotes, scaling relations, high-z structure…), survey/instrument entities, and per-topic annotated bibliographies, every citation verified.
- [ROADMAP.md](./ROADMAP.md): what this assistant does not do yet and why — benchmark calibration, a second instrument's dataset, two ungrounded skills, upstream fixes to contribute. Nothing in the repo links to an item on it.

## Runnable examples & tutorials (elsewhere)

- [autogalaxy_workspace navigator](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autogalaxy_workspace/blob/main/llms.txt): task router for end-to-end example scripts and notebooks. This is the grounding truth for the API — prefer it over memory every time.
- [HowToGalaxy](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/HowToGalaxy): from-first-principles galaxy-morphology lecture series, in five chapters from grids and light profiles through modelling, search chaining and pixelisations.
